patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

Secondary_Symptoms: Not oriented to time and space
Jaundice on the skin and mucous membranes

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with agitation, yellowish coloring of the skin and eyes, and abnormal lab findings.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Doctor, for the past 24 hours I’ve been feeling very agitated and restless, and I’m not really oriented to time or where I am. My family also says I’ve looked yellow in my skin and eyes over the last week, and I’ve had some nosebleeds.”
[ASK] Do you have **vertigo (a spinning sensation)** that is triggered by **changing head position** (e.g., rolling in bed or looking up/down)?
“No, I don’t feel spinning or vertigo with head movement, and it doesn’t seem to be related to turning my head or changing positions.”
[ASK] Do you have a history of **recurrent wheezing or shortness of breath** (asthma/COPD-type symptoms)?
“No, I haven’t had recurrent wheezing or shortness of breath—no asthma or COPD-type symptoms that I’m aware of.”
[ASK] Do you have involuntary movements or progressive neurologic decline consistent with Parkinson disease (e.g., resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia)?
“No—I don’t have a resting tremor, stiffness/rigidity, or slow movements like Parkinson’s, and I haven’t noticed any progressive decline beyond this sudden agitation and confusion.”
[ASK] Do you have eye pain or redness (suggesting keratitis)?
“No, I haven’t had any eye pain or redness. Mostly it’s just that I look yellow in my eyes and skin, and I’ve been very agitated and confused.”
[ASK] Do you currently have a rash or skin lesions (any new or worsening spots, blisters, or sores)?
“No, I haven’t noticed any new rash, blisters, or skin sores—just the yellowing of my skin and eyes. I also haven’t noticed any painful or worsening spots.”
[ASK] Have you had **new neurologic symptoms** such as weakness, numbness, seizures, or progressive neurologic decline?
“No—before this started I didn’t have weakness or numbness, and I haven’t had any seizures. It’s mainly the sudden agitation and confusion with me not being oriented to time or where I am.”
[ASK] Do you have **fever** (or chills) suggesting an active infection/inflammation?
“No, I haven’t had any fever or chills. It’s mostly been sudden agitation and confusion, along with the yellowing my family noticed and some nosebleeds.”
[ASK] Have you had episodes of fainting (passing out) or near-fainting (lightheadedness with loss of consciousness)?
“No, I haven’t fainted or nearly fainted, and I haven’t lost consciousness at any point—I’ve mainly been awake but very agitated and confused.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **Toxic exposure**?

“Doctor, I have used cocaine and ecstasy occasionally, and I drink alcohol socially on weekends—but I don’t know of any other toxic exposure. I don’t have any other exposures like chemicals or medications that could be new.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **Toxic exposure**?

“Doctor, the only exposures I can think of are occasional cocaine and ecstasy, and I had alcohol socially on weekends—but I don’t know of any other toxic chemicals or new medications. I also haven’t noticed any new rash or fever.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **Toxic exposure**?

“Doctor, I don’t think I’ve had any other toxic exposure besides occasional cocaine and ecstasy, and alcohol on weekends. I haven’t taken any new medications or chemicals that I’m aware of, and I don’t remember any unusual substances.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **Toxic exposure**?

“Doctor, I haven’t had any other known toxic exposures besides occasional cocaine and ecstasy and some weekend alcohol, and I don’t recall any unusual substances. I also haven’t taken any new medications or chemicals that I’m aware of.”
[ASK] Are you experiencing **Toxic exposure**?

“Doctor, yes—I’ve only had occasional cocaine and ecstasy, plus some alcohol on weekends. I don’t recall any other medications, chemicals, or unusual substances beyond that, but I can’t be completely certain what’s in everything I used.”
